summary: Josho Nozawa worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under Susumu Yamaguchi. He held a professorship at Koyasan University, attested in 1950.
Joshua Ereshefsky works in Buddhist and religious studies. Attested in 2026, he is a PhD candidate in religious studies at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn.
Joshua Marshman was a scholar of Sinology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at Bristol Baptist College (~1794–1799) and under Johannes Lassar (~1805–1812), and founded Serampore College in 1818.

Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who earned his BA at Yale (~1989–1993), MA at Oxford (~1993), and PhD at Harvard (~1995–1998). He served as Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022).
Joshua W. C. Cutler specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. A student of Geshe Wangyal, he held a post at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center, attested in 2004.

Josiah Royce was a philosopher who studied at the University of California (~1871–1875), University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze (~1875–1876), and Johns Hopkins University (~1876–1878). He served on the faculty at Harvard University from 1882 to 1916.

José Ignacio Cabezón works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1978–1986) under Geshe Lhundub Sopa and became the Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby, attested in 2012.

Jowita Kramer specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She completed her dissertation under Lambert Schmithausen at the University of Hamburg (~2000–2004) and her Habilitation at Munich (~2005–2010), becoming a professor at the University of Leipzig in 2021.

Joy Cecile Brennan is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology who completed her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard A. Rosengarten, and Constance Furey.

Joyce Burkhalter Flueckiger is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Goshen College (~1970–1974) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1974–1984). She served at Emory University (~1991–2022), where she became Professor Emerita.
Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under the supervision of Max Deeg, attested in 2012.

Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who completed her DPhil at the University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1993–1999). She taught as an associate professor at the University of Lille (2001) and became a professor at EPHE in 2018.

Judith Simmer-Brown works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, completing her PhD at Walden University (~1975–1978) and studying under Chögyam Trungpa. In 1977, she joined Naropa University, later becoming Distinguished Professor Emerita.

Juha Pentikäinen is a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1960–1963) and the University of Turku (~1963–1968). He served as Professor of Comparative Religion at the University of Helsinki (~1972–2008).

Juhn Young Ahn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley (ended 2007). He was attested in 2019 as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies at the University of Michigan.

Juhyung Rhi specializes in Buddhist studies and art history/archaeology, receiving a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. In 1992, he became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University.
Juichiro Tanabe was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and studied under the traditional teacher Richard Hunn.
Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon College. He served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

Jules Bloch was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. He held posts as directeur d’études at EPHE (1919–1951) and Chair of Sanskrit language and literature at the Collège de France (1936–1951).
